solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make a fuss about extreme hike in tariff

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for tariff

parts.note: a tariff is a rate charged

indicators.note: the extreme of a word here is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about a steep rise in charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme hike' is the E at the end of hike, and 'in' puts it inside RATE to give REATE after C.
explanation.definitionFit: To create, in British informal use, is to make a scene or kick up a fuss.

clue.text: Channel Islands School of Buddhism's feeding its poor residents

indicators.note: feeding means the Buddhist school goes inside the other letters
poor means the little word its is in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Zen school in Jersey or Guernsey is feeding its needy inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Buddhism's stands for 'is', so the school is what does the feeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens are the inhabitants of a town or country, its residents.

clue.text: Circulating salient points in advance is crucial

indicators.note: in advance says the compass letters come first

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south

indicators.note: circulating sends the letters of salient round into a new order

explanation.surface: Sending out the key points beforehand is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salient points' reads as a phrase, but salient is the fodder and points gives ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means absolutely necessary, the same as crucial.

clue.text: Arrange minute with daughter instead of partner

indicators.note: instead of means one letter is swapped in for the other

parts.note: minute means very small
N is north, partner of south at bridge

explanation.surface: Fix a time with your daughter in place of your spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' is the adjective (my-NEWT), not sixty seconds. N comes from bridge, where North and South are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy is to put things in order, to arrange them neatly.

clue.text: Bypass work's held back by lazy person

indicators.note: held means the lazy person's word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a skiver is British slang for someone who dodges work

indicators.note: back means the short word for work is read the other way round

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A detour is delayed by someone idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the work and 'held' puts it inside the lazy person; a skiver is British slang for a shirker.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip over something is to omit or pass it by, the same as bypassing it.

clue.text: I'm not sure what to say after spy's set up by M so stay quiet

indicators.note: after says the hesitation sound follows
set up in a down clue means the spying word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to peek is to spy or peep

parts.words: I'm not sure what to say
parts.note: um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A spy set up by M, the spymaster, decides to say nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the head of MI6 in the Bond films, but here it is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is an idiom meaning to stay silent and say nothing.

clue.text: Performance fades out before men stripped — didn't risk it!

indicators.note: before says the rearranged letters precede the last piece

parts.note: a play is a theatrical performance

indicators.note: out means the letters of fades are put out of order
stripped means the word men loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A show fades out before the cast strip off, so nobody took a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fades out' reads as a theatre phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal; 'men stripped' leaves only its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To play safe is an idiom for avoiding risk and taking the cautious option.

clue.text: Suspect diva, soft at heart, is lacking charisma

indicators.note: at heart puts the soft letter in the middle
suspect means dubious, so the letters of diva are reordered

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for soft

explanation.surface: A questionable prima donna, gentle underneath, has no stage presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' rearranges DIVA as VAID, and P sits at its heart: VA-P-ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapid means dull and flat, lacking liveliness or interest.

clue.text: Without water supply year after river under bridge finally disappeared

indicators.note: after says the year letter follows
disappeared means that letter vanishes from the word under
finally picks out the last letter of bridge

explanation.surface: A year after the river beneath the bridge finally vanished, there was no water.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDER loses the E that ends 'bridge', giving UNDR.
explanation.definitionFit: A well or tap that has run dry has no water left in it, as in 'the taps have run dry'.

clue.text: Focus on chance to nurse rising team

indicators.note: to nurse means to hold close, so fate wraps around the other piece

parts.note: fate means chance or fortune

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the team's letters read upwards

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Fortune is looking after a team that is on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns XI into IX, which FATE 'nurses': F-IX-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fixate is to fix one's attention obsessively, to concentrate on.

clue.text: After cricket match will try out new car

indicators.note: After says the word for will follows the cricket word

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
will and drive both mean determination

explanation.surface: Once the cricket is over, someone plans to try a new car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning determination.
explanation.definitionFit: A test drive is a trial run in a vehicle before buying it.

clue.text: First class get special enclosure in US ski resort

parts.note: A is the letter for first class, as in A1
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A first-class guest gets a special roped-off area at a ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen in Colorado is a famous American skiing town.

clue.text: Oddly comical sample of Tarzan yell

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snippet of Tarzan's famous jungle cry is strangely funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany means absurdly or eccentrically funny, comical in an odd way.

clue.text: Friend made error perhaps, or not, seeing fortune teller

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: perhaps says the remaining letters may be rearranged
or not means the letters of the word or are left out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend blundered, or maybe not, when visiting a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or not' strips the last two letters of error, leaving MADEERR for 'perhaps' to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmist foretells the future from the lines on the hand, a kind of fortune teller.

clue.text: Commanding Officer with military police is more unlikely to negotiate

indicators.note: unlikely means the letters of is more are in an improbable order

explanation.surface: An army commander alongside the redcaps is less inclined to bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise is to settle by mutual concession, which is what negotiating aims for.

clue.text: Row about retired doctor is hurtful

indicators.note: about means the row's word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a row is a loud noise

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the doctor's letters go backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: An argument about a retired GP is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, a din, not a line; 'retired' reverses the doctor and 'about' wraps the din round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means harmful or offensive; hurtful is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Question's dividing some running temple

indicators.note: dividing means the question piece splits the other letters
running means the letters of some are set loose and reordered

explanation.surface: A question splits some joggers at a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges SOME as MOSE, and 'dividing' puts QU in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosque is a Muslim place of worship, broadly a temple.

clue.text: Not sure a French church has central heating during wet weather

parts.note: un is French for a
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: during means the middle letter sits inside the weather word

parts.note: rain is wet weather

indicators.note: central picks the middle letter of heating

explanation.surface: A French church with central heating is doubtful in rainy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central heating' looks like the radiator system but gives T, the middle letter of heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain means doubtful or unsure.

clue.text: Kind of insect outside bothered diner

indicators.note: outside means the insect wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a fly is an insect

indicators.note: bothered means flustered, so the letters of diner are mixed up

explanation.surface: An insect outside pesters a restaurant customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' rearranges DINER as RIEND, which FLY goes 'outside': F-RIEND-LY. 'Kind of' looks like a phrase but 'Kind' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly means kind, warm and well-disposed.

clue.text: Bloomer showing when underskirt's not pulled down?

definitions.meaning: a bloomer is a blunder or mistake

definitions.text: showing when underskirt's not pulled down?
definitions.meaning: a petticoat, or slip, that has ridden up is on show

explanation.surface: Bloomers show when a petticoat rides up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests underwear to match the underskirt, but it is the British word for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a small mistake, which is exactly a bloomer; the second reading is a slip lifted up.

clue.text: Grassland in Peru regularly windy we hear

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the country name
we hear means the breezy word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: airy means breezy, windy

explanation.surface: Peruvian grasslands are often gusty.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast open plain of grass, especially in North America.

clue.text: Aristocrat, losing head taking diamonds, has run into policeman

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the aristocrat's word is dropped

parts.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class person
ice is slang for diamonds
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A beheaded noble grabbing jewels has bumped into a cop.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF, British slang for a posh person, 'losing head' becomes OFF; then ICE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is a member of the force, a policeman.

clue.text: Good to leave gold and silver with last relative in final years

indicators.note: to leave means the good letter departs from gold

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of relative

explanation.surface: A dying wish: let the gold go and leave the silver to the last relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Old age is the closing period of a life, its final years.

clue.text: Cool group of women on deck at sea

parts.note: the WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of deck are jumbled

explanation.surface: A women's club on a ship's deck is having a great time.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women; 'at sea' rearranges DECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked is slang for excellent, just as cool is.

clue.text: Under threat of early finish, open-air DJ set goes ahead

indicators.note: goes ahead says the rearranged letters come before the final letter
set means the letters are arranged in a new order
the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Fearing an early finish, an outdoor DJ performance proceeds anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges OPENAIRDJ to INJEOPARD, which 'goes ahead' of Y, the finish of 'early'. 'set' looks like a DJ's set.
explanation.definitionFit: In jeopardy means in danger or at risk.

clue.text: Frenchman's trousers?

definitions.meaning: belonging to Jean, a French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as JEAN'S it means belonging to a Frenchman called Jean; as one word it is the denim garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim garments for the legs are a type of trousers; Jean is a common French name.

clue.text: Time to regret being honest

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: It's time to be sorry for telling the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean sincere and faithful, an honest person.

clue.text: Inspire uplifting in spirits

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the found letters read upwards
in means the letters are found inside the word spirits

explanation.surface: Something uplifting raises the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' looks like praise, but it reverses RITS, found in sp-IRITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to rouse or move someone emotionally, to inspire.

clue.text: Vehicle guide picked up is a muddy colour

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the phrase is said and not written

parts.note: a car is a vehicle; a key is a guide, as to a map or puzzle

explanation.surface: A safari vehicle's guide is collected from a muddy track.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, car key and the colour word sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow shade, the colour of dust and mud.

clue.text: One side gets help pursuing justice

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so help comes after justice

parts.note: right means what is just
a hand is help

explanation.surface: A campaigner gets assistance in seeking justice.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand side is one of the two sides of anything.

clue.text: Make a mess of translating "She-Devil"

indicators.note: translating converts the letters of the quoted title into a different form

explanation.surface: A translator botches the title of a novel or film.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel is to rumple or disorder hair or clothing, to make untidy.

clue.text: Up for sex after final Jägerbomb drink

indicators.note: after says the lustful word follows that letter
final picks out the last letter of the drink's name

parts.note: randy means lustful, keen for sex

explanation.surface: Someone is feeling frisky after their last shot of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jägerbomb is a shot of Jägermeister dropped into an energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an alcoholic drink.
